evidence: The reading view always runs immersive (web/panel.html:511), and web/panel.html:106 hides every child of #view-reading except the page and the menu. Measured in Chromium: #reader-pager and .reader-pager-overlay both compute to display:none in that state, so no page-turn control is ever visible and no copy says arrow keys turn the page; the design artifact docs/design-immersive-reading.html:79 carried exactly that hint ("← → turn the page") and the live tree dropped it. #reader-note also computes to none, so the per-page message at panel.html:902 ("This page did not read cleanly, so this is the page itself.") can never be seen — the picture replaces the text with no stated trigger.
fix: Restore the design's hint inside #reader (a muted "← → turn the page" line), and exclude .reader-pager-overlay, #reader-note, .arrival-note, .latency-chip and .forfeit-note from the panel.html:106 hide rule (add them to the :not() chain or scope the rule to > .view-chrome) so the pager and the per-page message render in immersive mode.

evidence: The reading screen is the one screen whose primary ask (turn the page and keep reading) is never stated. In immersive mode, measured in Chromium, #reader-pager, .reader-pager-overlay and #reader-note are all display:none (web/panel.html:106, 118-127), leaving one unlabelled "⋯" button (web/panel.html:429) and no imperative anywhere. The to-do screen (web/panel.html:470) likewise states only "Read only. Ticking here is tracked by Interstice and never edits the note." and never asks the reader to tick anything.
fix: Add to the reading view, visible in immersive mode: "Press → for the next page, ← to go back. Everything else is behind ⋯." Add to the to-do view: "Tick anything you have already done. Interstice keeps the tick; your note is never changed."

evidence: web/panel.html:1231-1232 renders "39% · position 3,214 of 8,190 · ASIN B0..." under the book title: "ASIN" is an unexpanded abbreviation the reader is meant to do nothing with, and "position" gives no unit. web/panel.html:1028 appends "  ·  2 ready" to the page label, an orphan count with nothing saying what is ready or why it matters. web/dashboard.html:254 shows "Gaps below threshold" without naming the threshold (25s, from config).

evidence: web/panel.html:427 renders "Response landed" on a surface that shows a book page: no response, prompt, session or agent is named anywhere in panel.html, so the definite noun has nothing to resolve to. web/panel.html:1028 renders "2 ready" with no antecedent for "ready". web/dashboard.html:128 says "Next rung" on a page that never defines a rung.

evidence: web/panel.html:990-994 is a four-sentence block whose first sentence runs 26 words around an embedded quote ("Amazon’s reader answered with “Please try to open this book from the library again”, which it says whether or not the book came from the library.") and whose third assumes the reader knows what "this reader’s registration as a device" is. web/panel.html:600-602 packs two ideas into one line ("4 reviews per due card, the lowest of 7 decks with anything due · 12 due here of 96 overall"), and web/panel.html:1251-1253 tells the reader to answer a prompt about "node".

Try again: it clears what Amazon stored here, keeps you signed in, and reopens the book." panel.html:600 -> "Fewest reviews per due card of your 7 decks with work waiting." then on its own line "12 of your 96 due cards are here." panel.html:1251 -> name the app the reader sees, not "node".

evidence: Raw internal reason codes reach the screen verbatim: web/panel.html:578-579 sets deck-why to String(d.reason) when Anki is unreachable, web/panel.html:1254 does the same for any unmapped book reason, and web/panel.html:1387 falls back to String(d.reason) for to-do lists, so strings such as "no_due_cards" or "AnkiConnect unreachable: fetch failed" are shown as the explanation. web/panel.html:621-622 explains the button in terms of the product's internals ("turns off App Nap, and waits for AnkiConnect to answer").
fix: panel.html:578/1254/1387 -> map every reason code to a reader-facing sentence and use a single generic fallback ("Interstice could not read your cards. Press Reconnect to Anki.") while logging the raw code to /debug. panel.html:621 -> "Wakes Anki in the background and waits for it. Nothing comes to the front."

evidence: Thought-flow map, built first: [presses enter on a prompt] -> "right, that will be a few minutes"; [the panel appears unasked, bottom right] -> "why is this here, and how long do I have?"; [sees a deck or a book page] -> "am I going to get yanked out of this mid-card?"; [reads] -> "is it done yet?"; [agent finishes] -> "was that my prompt or something else?". FINDINGS: the question held at arrival and again while reading goes unanswered anywhere in the flow — no user-facing string in web/panel.html names the agent, the prompt, the session or the gap (grep for agent/prompt over the rendered strings returns only CSS gap and the queue box), and the one arrival signal, "Response landed" (web/panel.html:427), never renders: it is a child of #view-reading, which is display:none outside the reading view and whose children except the page and menu are hidden by web/panel.html:106 (measured display:none in Chromium).
fix: Put a persistent line in the panel header naming the reason it opened and the live elapsed time, e.g. "Claude Code has been working 2m 14s". Make the arrival notification render (exclude .arrival-note from the panel.html:106 hide rule) and give it a referent: "Your Claude Code answer is ready."

evidence: The reading surface is the densest text in the product (a full page of prose), and #book-actions still renders under it in immersive mode: measured display:flex in Chromium, because the inline style at web/panel.html:424 outranks the hide rule at web/panel.html:106. It carries the shelf list ("Or another one you have going", web/panel.html:1274) and the aside "Amazon’s own reader is drawing this, in a browser you never see, at the page your Kindle synced to. Open the Kindle app instead." (web/panel.html:1280-1281). Neither supports any decision the reader is making while reading, and both eat the page area the design promises at >=90% (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:82). Second, smaller offender: the sign-in block repeats its own reassurance across two paragraphs (web/panel.html:1088-1095).
fix: Move #book-actions behind the ⋯ menu with the other displaced chrome (drop the inline display:flex at panel.html:424 so the panel.html:106 rule applies, and it is already in READER_MENU_DISPLACED at panel.html:1697). Cut the second sign-in paragraph down to "Only works while your own Chrome is still signed in to Amazon." (panel.html:1093-1095).

evidence: No Chart.js anywhere in the target: grep for "Chart.js", "new Chart(", "maintainAspectRatio" and "<canvas" over web/, lib/, docs/ and README.md matches only the audit rule text under docs/audit/. Every visualisation here is hand-built DOM (web/dashboard.html:237-239 bar rows, web/panel.html:1877-1890 calendar grid), so the rule has no instance to apply to.

CONDITIONAL. Precondition: a palette or design-token rename shipped (the batch records it as "applies only if phase 2 introduces a token layer"). It did NOT hold in this repo: git show over the phase 2-5 commits (d0613a1, d8ec9be, fdfb5bf, 9949966) shows zero added, removed or renamed CSS custom properties in web/panel.html, and the panel's :root block at web/panel.html:9-18 is unchanged since commit e7f55a7. The only rename in the period is a localStorage key, MODE_KEY = "interstice.readerMode.v2" (web/panel.html:765), which is not a design token.

The direction is deliberate overall: Charter/Iowan Old Style serif body with condensed uppercase micro-labels (web/panel.html:24, 38, 200), one accent per theme (web/panel.html:9-18), a shimmer plus spinner motion vocabulary with a reduced-motion guard (web/panel.html:303-315), and no UI framework at all. The phase 3-5 additions were left on the platform default font instead: web/panel.html:159 (.forfeit-note), :180 (.cal-dow), :191 (.cal-reveal), :193 (.cal-legend) and :196 (.cal-empty-copy) all specify system-ui, so the forfeit banner and the whole star calendar read as untyped system chrome next to the rest of the panel, and they contradict the design artifact, which sets the same calendar in Avenir Next Condensed and Charter (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:51-57).
fix: Replace system-ui in panel.html:159, 180, 191, 193 and 196 with the panel's own pairing: "Avenir Next Condensed", "Avenir Next", sans-serif for the calendar micro-labels and Charter, "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif for the reveal and forfeit copy.

evidence: There is no single token architecture: web/panel.html:9-18 declares a 9-token palette while web/dashboard.html:8-24 declares a different 15-token one, with different values for the same names (--ground #F1F3F5 vs #EEF0F2, --warn #A8620F vs #9A6A12) and type tokens (--display/--body/--mono) that the panel does not have at all, so every font stack in panel.html is a literal repeated by hand. Hardcoded values then bypass what tokens exist: web/panel.html:223 (button.act.primary color:#fff), web/panel.html:82 (#companions button.do color:#fff) and web/dashboard.html:62 (button.primary color:#fff) put white on var(--accent), which measures 7.06:1 in light theme but 2.71:1 in dark (#FFFFFF on #8296FF) — below even 3:1, and invisible to a per-theme contrast audit because the value is not a token. web/panel.html:212 (.cardframe iframe background:#fff) and web/panel.html:91 (.proof img background:#000) also do not follow the theme flip.
fix: Promote one token file shared by panel.html and dashboard.html (colour, type, spacing, radius), give it an --on-accent token defined per theme (#fff in light, a dark ink in dark) and replace the three color:#fff declarations with it, and replace the #fff/#000 surfaces at panel.html:212 and :91 with var(--raised) and var(--ink).

evidence:
The only iframe in the product is web/panel.html:545, an srcdoc document the panel composes itself from the Anki card plus that deck's stylesheet — not a third-party page. Amazon's reader is never framed; its page is fetched headless and the words are re-rendered in the panel's own type by default (web/panel.html:765-773 defaults the mode to text, web/panel.html:907-917 sets the blocks as the panel's own

/

), with the rendered picture as an explicit per-page fallback. The one live third-party surface is the Amazon sign-in page (web/panel.html:1037), which the rule exempts as a sign-in flow that must run on the provider's origin.

Two charts exist and both match their question. web/dashboard.html:237-239 answers "which rungs did it send me to, and how do they compare" with horizontal bars, the right form for a categorical comparison. web/panel.html:1877-1890 answers "when did I earn stars" with a month calendar grid, the right form for occurrence over dates. No pie chart, no dual axis and no 3D chart appears anywhere in the target.

Contrast is fine: measured against the plot backgrounds, --accent is 5.73:1 (light, on --sunk) and 6.76:1 (dark), and --ok/--warn/--crit are all above 3.8:1 in both themes. The categorical status palette does not survive colour-vision deficiency: under a Vienot deuteranopia simulation web/dashboard.html:12 --warn #9A6A12 renders #8A8E3E and --crit #A82B22 renders #8A9125 (RGB distance 0.10), and in dark theme (web/dashboard.html:22) #D6A44A and #E0736A render #C5C96F and #C0C76D (distance 0.02) — indistinguishable. Colour is the only encoding of severity on the false-positives tile (web/dashboard.html:204, 210) and on the verdict pills (web/dashboard.html:250-256), so a deuteranope cannot tell "warn" from "critical".
fix: Add a non-colour carrier to the same elements: give the pill its band as text ("warn" / "critical") in web/dashboard.html:261, or re-pick --crit to separate from --warn under deuteranopia (a blue-red such as #C0392B is not enough; a lightness split plus a leading glyph is).

evidence: Neither colour-encoded surface misuses a scale. The star calendar encodes a categorical present/absent — a day either carries star buttons or does not (web/panel.html:1887), all drawn in the one accent (web/panel.html:186-188), with multiplicity encoded by repeating the mark rather than by hue. The dashboard bars encode magnitude by length in a single hue (web/dashboard.html:83), not by a categorical palette. No diverging scale is used anywhere, and there is no dataset here with a meaningful midpoint that is missing one.

The bar chart labels every row on the left with the rung name and prints the exact count on the right (web/dashboard.html:238), states its unit in the section note ("N deliveries", web/dashboard.html:236), draws one series so no legend is owed, and scales from zero to the maximum (width n/max, web/dashboard.html:238) so no axis is truncated. The star calendar carries a legend saying what the mark means ("an earned 25-minute block", web/panel.html:449) and reveals the exact wall-clock start and end on click (web/panel.html:1844-1845), which is the tooltip requirement met.

The five tiles do not share one system. Unit placement differs across the same row: web/dashboard.html:208 puts the unit in the key ("Minutes reclaimed" over a bare number) while :209 puts it inside the value ("3m 54s" from fmtSec) and :210 inside the value again as a percent. Colour meaning differs too: web/dashboard.html:206 colours the Gaps tile "accent" decoratively while :210 colours the False positives tile ok/warn/crit semantically (fpClass, web/dashboard.html:204), so the reader cannot tell whether a coloured number is a status or a highlight. Numerals, tabular-nums treatment and the loading skeleton are consistent (web/dashboard.html:67, 135-139).
fix: Move every unit into the tile key ("Median turn (m:s)", "Minutes reclaimed", "False positives (%)") and leave the values bare, and drop the "accent" class from the Gaps tile at web/dashboard.html:206 so colour on a tile means status and nothing else.

evidence: The star calendar plots an unmeasured zero as a measured one. web/panel.html:1823-1827 _thisMonth() returns null when no stars are loaded, so the first open calls _loadStarCal(null), which at web/panel.html:1829 renders "No stars earned yet. Complete a 25-minute block to earn your first." (web/panel.html:1876) without ever calling /api/stars/month. When the fetch is attempted and fails, web/panel.html:1834 catches and renders the same empty month, and web/panel.html:1892 prints "No stars earned this month yet." — a reader cannot tell a genuinely starless month from a month that was never read. The dashboard does not have this defect: its empty state says so explicitly (web/dashboard.html:269-271).
fix: Derive the month from the client clock when no star is cached (new Date().toISOString().slice(0,7)) so _loadStarCal always queries, and give the catch at web/panel.html:1834 its own state — "Interstice could not read your stars. Try again." — visually distinct from the earned-zero copy at web/panel.html:1876 and :1892.

evidence: CONDITIONAL. Precondition: a Claude Design handoff bundle exists and docs/design-immersive-reading.html is the canonical string source. It does NOT hold: the repo's own selection manifest records "no Claude Design handoff bundle" (docs/GOAL_LOOP_STARS_READER_2026-08-17.md:693, docs/RECURRING_GOALS_SELECTION.md:61), and the artifact is a three-state visual mock with illustrative copy, not a string inventory, produced by the frontend-design/design-reference route prescribed at docs/GOAL_LOOP_STARS_READER_2026-08-17.md:371-373. Drift recorded as asked: the live panel does carry explanatory fallback strings the mock has no counterpart for ("This page did not read cleanly, so this is the page itself." web/panel.html:902; "· some of this page read poorly" web/panel.html:916; "Remembered from ... this position may have moved since" web/panel.html:1267-1269), but with no design bundle to diff against, those are judged by UFC-007 and UFC-009 above rather than as fidelity offences.

CONDITIONAL. Same precondition as DF-005, and it does NOT hold: there is no Claude Design export in the tree (docs/GOAL_LOOP_STARS_READER_2026-08-17.md:693). Drift recorded as asked, and it runs live-away-from-design in both directions: the design shows a persistent hint "← → turn the page" (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:79) that the live panel never renders; the design's rung labels are "Flashcards / Reading / Queue next / To-do" (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:93) while the live header reads "Cards / Book / Queue / To-do" (web/panel.html:324-327); the design promises the page at >=90% of both dimensions (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:82) while #book-actions still renders under the page in immersive mode (measured display:flex, inline style at web/panel.html:424); and the design's star detail reads "Star 1  09:12 → 09:37 (25m unbroken)" (docs/design-immersive-reading.html:115) against the live "A block earned on <day>: began X · ended Y" (web/panel.html:1844). No case was resolved by editing the design to match the code — the design file has not been touched since it was written.

The design slice did not go to Claude Design. docs/GOAL_LOOP_STARS_READER_2026-08-17.md:371-373 routes phase 2A.4 to the frontend-design, design-reference, dataviz and web-design-guidelines skills, and docs/design-immersive-reading.html is the hand-authored HTML that route produced; docs/RECURRING_GOALS_SELECTION.md:61 states the same ("no design/claude-design bundle; the design phase here uses frontend-design and design-reference"). Mitigating fact, recorded rather than used to soften the verdict: the artifact is nowhere labelled a Claude Design export, so it misrepresents nothing.
fix: Re-run the immersive-reading and star-calendar slices through Claude Design and let its export replace docs/design-immersive-reading.html as the canonical artifact, or amend the goal loop to state explicitly that this project takes the general-model design route so the rule is waived on the record rather than by omission.
